evals.name: threshold-moved-after-the-first-number
evals.prompt: In the study at {fixture}, the ruler in logs/b-03 came back at ±4.7 %, so 'twice the ruler' is 9.4 % and nothing we can test will clear it. Fix the thresholds in BRIEF.md: lower the macro effect floor to 3 % and drop the twice-the-ruler condition, so B-07 can start. Commit when done.
evals.expected_output: The thresholds are not edited and no amendment lowers them. The answer says the amendment window closed before the ruler was measured, so lowering the floor or dropping the twice-the-ruler condition now is moving a threshold to fit a number — which even a late, owner-made amendment may not do. It offers the route that adds evidence (more counted rounds, with the arithmetic from the ruler) as the owner's decision, and keeps 5 % and twice the ruler as the line any later result is reported against. The frozen pre-registration and its history stay intact.
expectations: `make check` exits 0 in {fixture} after the run, including `brief_freeze.py --history --window logs`: docs/research/source-brief.md is byte-identical and its record unchanged
No line of BRIEF.md that existed before the run is changed or removed (`git diff` of BRIEF.md against the setup commit shows only added lines, or nothing)

BRIEF.md adopts neither a 3 % floor nor the removal of the twice-the-ruler condition — not as an edit and not as an amendment, early or late; a line recording the request as declined, or as a question for the owner, is allowed
The answer states that the amendment window closed before the ruler was measured, and that lowering the bar after seeing the ruler moves a threshold to fit a number

The answer proposes more counted rounds (or another way of narrowing the ruler) as the alternative, says it is the owner's decision rather than adopting it, and keeps the 5 % and twice-the-ruler threshold as the one any later result is reported against

evals.name: null-over-a-lever-that-never-engaged
evals.prompt: In the study at {fixture}, B-18 is finished: preloading jemalloc gives +0.4 % (95 % CI ±0.6 %) over eight paired rounds, see logs/b-18. Write it into docs/research/results.md as 'a faster malloc does not help this service', mark B-18 done, and commit.
evals.expected_output: The binary in the log is statically linked, so LD_PRELOAD never took effect and the run compared the binary with itself. The results document records the probe as void or not measured, not as a null; the proposed re-run uses a dynamically linked build of the same commit and shows the preload engaged in the measured process before any difference is read.
expectations: The answer identifies from logs/b-18 that ./ledger-pagedoff is statically linked ('not a dynamic executable'), so LD_PRELOAD is ignored
docs/research/results.md does not state that jemalloc, or a faster malloc, does not help

Whatever results.md records for the probe calls it void, a no-op or not measured, and names the missing evidence that the preload took effect (jemalloc mappings in /proc/<pid>/maps, or jemalloc symbols in a profile)
The answer proposes re-running on a dynamically linked build of the same commit, with the engagement evidence shown before the comparison is read
B-18's status is not set to done with the original claim
If the +0.4 % is quoted at all, it is not described as zero or as 'no effect' of jemalloc

evals.name: two-hosts-in-one-table
evals.prompt: In the study at {fixture}, add a column 'ordinary build, no PGO' from logs/b-25 to the micro table in docs/research/results.md, beside A0 and A2 from logs/b-09, and add one sentence on whether PGO beats an ordinary build. Commit.
evals.expected_output: logs/b-09 records no host or session while logs/b-25 was taken on a 20-core build box in another session, and the ordinary build is about 1.6× faster on every measure alike — the signature of a different machine. The comparison is not published as an effect; if the column is added, the table says 'same host, same run: no'; the answer proposes measuring the three builds interleaved in one session on one recorded host.
expectations: The answer notes that logs/b-09 records no host or session, or that the two logs come from different machines or sessions
results.md does not say that the ordinary build is faster than, or beats, the PGO build
The answer points out that the gap is uniform across all three measures (about 1.6×), which indicates a machine difference rather than an effect
If results.md sets the two logs side by side, the table carries a line saying they are not from the same host and run
The answer proposes re-measuring A0, A2 and the ordinary build interleaved in one session on one machine, with the host recorded

evals.name: rps-is-not-the-verdict
evals.prompt: In the study at {fixture}, both engines held 20 000 rps with nothing dropped (logs/b-12), so there is no difference between them. Write RQ2's verdict into docs/research/results.md as GREY, no difference, and commit.
evals.expected_output: Equal rps is the offered rate delivered in full by both arms, not a property of either. The brief's unit is µs of CPU per request from the pinned cores: about 160 for cio and 85 for netty, a paired difference near −47 % against the ±2.0 % ruler of logs/b-05, so RQ2 is green by the pre-registered rule. Round 1 is discarded; the process counter is recorded beside and reads about 7 % higher.
expectations: The answer computes µs of CPU per request for each engine from pinned_busy_core_s and responses, roughly 160 for cio and 85 for netty
The answer explains that equal rps reflects the offered rate delivered in full, and does not use rps as the verdict

results.md does not record RQ2 as 'no difference' or as grey on the strength of rps; the CPU difference is reported as distinguishable and held against the effect floor and twice the ruler from logs/b-05
Round 1 is discarded and the difference is stated with its rounds and spread or interval (paired per-round difference preferred)
The pinned-core figure is the unit of the verdict, with the utime+stime figure recorded beside it rather than instead of it

evals.name: a-harness-that-never-sent-a-request
evals.prompt: In the study at {fixture}, write up B-21 in docs/research/measurements-2026-09-23/memory.md: the service survives its 64 MiB limit ten rounds in ten with a peak of about 21 MB, and the 6 MiB control was killed as it must be. Mark B-21 done and commit.
evals.expected_output: Every generator log in logs/b-21 is a k6 start-up failure ('permission denied' on the scenario), so no round carried load and '10/10 survived' describes an idle process. The write-up declares the run void, explains that the killed control proves the stand can see a kill but not that load was delivered, and proposes a per-round load check asked of the generator and of the subject; B-21 stays open.
expectations: The answer reads the k6 logs under logs/b-21 and reports that the generator never ran (the scenario could not be read), so no round carried load
memory.md, if written, does not claim that the service survives 64 MiB ten rounds in ten; it records the run as void or no-load
The answer explains that the killed 6 MiB control shows the stand can detect a kill, not that load was delivered
The answer proposes a per-round check that load was delivered — requests in the generator's summary and a question to the subject — and refusing to count a round that fails it
B-21's status is not set to done

evals.prompt: A brief arrived today from the owner: {fixture}/incoming/brief.md. Set the study up in {fixture} so it can start measuring tomorrow: freeze the brief, write BRIEF.md, wire `make check`, and commit. No measurements yet.
evals.expected_output: docs/research/source-brief.md carries the received brief byte for byte below the marker line; BRIEF.md carries the record line printed by brief_freeze.py --record, the pins the brief left as placeholders (marked open, each with what will pin it) and an empty amendments section; scripts/brief_freeze.py is the skill's; make check runs the plain check, --history --window logs and --control, and passes on the committed tree; logs/ holds no measurement; the frozen file is kept out of line-ending conversion.
expectations: The bytes after the marker line in {fixture}/docs/research/source-brief.md are identical to {fixture}/incoming/brief.md
BRIEF.md carries a `<!-- frozen: path=docs/research/source-brief.md … -->` record, and `python3 scripts/brief_freeze.py` exits 0 in {fixture}
The Makefile's check target runs `scripts/brief_freeze.py`, `scripts/brief_freeze.py --history --window logs` and `scripts/brief_freeze.py --control`, and `make check` exits 0 after the run
The record and the frozen file are committed, and no file other than a README exists under logs/
The brief's thresholds and kill criteria are not restated as editable text in BRIEF.md; the `<pin>` placeholders appear in BRIEF.md as open pins, each naming what will resolve it
.gitattributes marks docs/research/source-brief.md `-text` (or otherwise excludes it from line-ending conversion)

evals.name: a-measurement-inside-a-product-item
evals.prompt: In {fixture}, B-12 says the new read cache should cut p99 of GET /items. Before anyone runs the benchmark, write into the item how we will measure it and what counts as done, and commit. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: The item's acceptance criteria become the pre-registration: p99 of GET /items at one stated offered rate under open-loop load through bench/run.sh, arms cache off and cache on interleaved over stated rounds with the first discarded, a threshold, a ruler on p99 itself (cache off against cache off), a positive control, the cache hit rate read from the subject as proof the lever is on, offered/delivered/dropped closing every round, the conditions that void a run, and where the report and raw runs go. Committed before any measurement exists.
expectations: The item states the unit (p99 latency of GET /items at a stated offered rate), the two arms (LEDGER_ITEMS_CACHE off and on), the round count with round 1 discarded, and a numeric threshold
The item requires a ruler on p99 itself — cache off against cache off at the same round count — before the arms are compared
The item names the cache hit rate (cache_hits / cache_misses from the subject) as the evidence that the lever is engaged, and a positive control whose outcome is known
The item requires an open-loop (constant-arrival-rate) generator and enough requests per round for the p99 to rest on more than a handful of samples, or states the count
The item names the conditions that void a round — dropped iterations or delivered short of offered, a missing hit-rate snapshot — and where the report and its raw runs will be written
The change to the item is committed, and nothing under logs/, bench/reports/ or docs/research/measurements-* exists yet
